memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then Joshua said to Achan, "My son, give glory to the Lord, the God of Israel, and honor him. Tell me what you have done; do not hide it from me." — Josh 7:19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice how Joshua speaks to Achan, even now. He does not scream or hurl abuse. He says, "My son." There is tenderness in the confrontation. Joshua treats this guilty man with dignity, appealing to him gently even as the truth must come out. This is a beautiful model for how to confront wrongdoing — firmly, but with compassion, never crushing the person beyond what is needed.

But look at the striking phrase Joshua uses: "Give glory to the Lord... Tell me what you have done." Confession, Joshua says, actually gives glory to God. How can admitting our sin bring God glory? Because honest confession agrees with God's assessment. It says, "God is right, and I was wrong. God's ways are true, and my ways were sinful." When we confess, we honour God's holiness and His truthfulness. Hiding sin, by contrast, calls God a liar; confession declares Him right.

This turns our thinking upside down. We often feel that confessing sin is shameful and dishonouring. But Scripture says the opposite: confession honours God. There is no shame in admitting the truth before the One who already knows it and stands ready to forgive.

The New Testament echoes this beautiful truth: "If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just and will forgive us our sins" (1 John 1:9). Confession is not groveling in defeat; it is glorifying God by agreeing with Him. And through Christ, that honest word of confession opens the door to full and free forgiveness.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you see confession as shameful, or as a way of giving glory to God?
2. When you confront others' wrongs, do you do so with the tenderness Joshua showed?
3. Is there a confession God is inviting you to make that would honour Him?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, help me see confession as glorifying You — agreeing that You are right and I am wrong. Give me a tender heart toward others, and honesty before You. Amen.
